sources.entry: Cyberduck - Cyberduck is a libre server and cloud storage browser for Mac and Windows with support for FTP, SFTP, WebDAV, Amazon S3, OpenStack Swift, Backblaze B2, Microsoft Azure & OneDrive, Google Drive and Dropbox.

summary.one_liner: Cyberduck is a libre file transfer client for macOS and Windows, with a CLI for Linux, macOS and Windows, and its development home repository.
summary.what_it_does: This repository is the development home for Cyberduck, a file transfer client for macOS and Windows. It also contains the source for the command line interface (CLI) that the README says runs on Linux, macOS and Windows. The README says the core libraries are used in Mountain Duck. Builds are produced with Maven and Ant, with a SKIP_SIGN option to skip code signing and a -Pinstaller profile that packages .app, .exe, .msi, .pkg, .deb and .rpm artifacts. Maven artifacts for protocol implementations and the core libraries are hosted in an Amazon S3 repository. User documentation, extra connection profiles and translations are maintained in separate resources, according to the README. The README does not list the protocols itself; the protocol list comes from the metadata line supplied with this listing.
use_cases: transfer files to FTP or SFTP servers on macOS or Windows
browse and manage cloud storage buckets and drives
use a command line file transfer tool on Linux, macOS or Windows
package installers for macOS and Windows
embed Cyberduck protocol libraries in a Java project
how_to_run: Install Java 11 SDK or later, Apache Ant 1.10.1 or later and Apache Maven 3.5 or later
On macOS, install Xcode 12 or later
On Windows, install Visual Studio 2022 with the required workloads, plus the Bonjour SDK
Find build artifacts in osx/target/Cyberduck.app or windows/target/Cyberduck.exe
Add -Pinstaller to the Maven command to build installer packages
notable: Shared core libraries are reused in Mountain Duck, according to the README
Includes a CLI that the README says runs on Linux, macOS and Windows
Maven artifacts for protocol implementations are published under GPL
Localized into roughly 30 languages through Transifex
Build profiles for code signing, macOS sandboxing and debugging
caveats: Windows builds need Visual Studio 2022, a GitHub Packages token for NuGet, and several components; the README notes Chocolatey installs may fail
Snapshot and beta builds are described as potentially unstable and experimental
Visual Studio cannot fully handle Java projects, so debugging on Windows needs extra steps
